title: Console API: create and query Shadow Experiments (CRUD, aggregates, example sampling) with RBAC
creator: Dylan Brooks
project: Shadow traffic tool for eval metrics
description:
Goal
Implement the Console backend API surface for Shadow Experiments so the Console UI and SDKs can:
- Create/update/delete shadow experiments attached to routes and/or rollouts
- Query experiment status, targets, and sampling config
- Fetch aggregated quality deltas (with confidence intervals) and core health counters
- Fetch sampled examples (prompt/response pairs + score breakdown) in a cardinality-safe and privacy-safe way
- Enforce RBAC/tenant boundaries and audit relevant actions

Context
Shadow traffic duplicates a sampled subset of production requests to one or more candidate variants (“shadow targets”) while returning the control response to the user. Shadow outputs are scored asynchronously (eval-harness adapter + rubric runner) and results are surfaced in Console alongside latency/cost/error metrics.

Non-goals (this ticket)
- Implement routing/mirroring in the data plane (ENG-5402)
- Implement telemetry ingestion/event schemas (ENG-5404)
- Implement scoring pipeline mechanics (ENG-5405/ENG-5406)
- Build UI pages (ENG-5408)

API shape (v1)
Note: exact route prefix may vary based on Console gateway conventions; below uses /v1/console for clarity.

1) CRUD
- POST /v1/console/shadow-experiments
  - Creates a shadow experiment definition.
  - Required inputs:
    - tenant_id (derived from auth context)
    - display_name
    - route_id OR rollout_id (at least one)
    - control: (implicitly the live route config at time of run; stored as a snapshot ref for auditability)
    - shadow_targets: list of variant refs (model_id/model_version OR policy_variant_id depending on rollout integration)
    - sampling: percent + bucketing salt/seed policy (seed stored, salt derived from tenant + experiment id)
    - fail_open: true (hard default; can’t be disabled in v1)
    - retention_profile: default (short) or dedicated/private override (validated)
  - Validations:
    - sampling_percent must be within [0.1, 20] by default (hard cap configurable per tenant; see guardrails)
    - max shadow targets: 3 (v1)
    - cannot target same variant as control snapshot
    - must match route request type constraints (chat vs completions vs embeddings)
    - streaming requests allowed only if shadow_streaming_mode is supported for the route (see ENG-5414)

- GET /v1/console/shadow-experiments
  - List experiments for a tenant.
  - Filters:
    - status (draft/running/paused/stopped)
    - route_id
    - rollout_id
    - created_by
    - updated_at range
  - Pagination:
    - cursor-based (opaque cursor) + limit (default 25, max 100)

- GET /v1/console/shadow-experiments/{experiment_id}
  - Returns experiment definition + current state.

- PATCH /v1/console/shadow-experiments/{experiment_id}
  - Allows updates to:
    - display_name, description
    - sampling_percent (within guardrails)
    - paused flag
    - shadow_targets (restricted; requires “experiment:editTargets” permission)
  - Immutable after start:
    - route_id/rollout_id binding
    - bucketing seed

- DELETE /v1/console/shadow-experiments/{experiment_id}
  - Soft-delete (archival) in v1; actual artifacts are handled by retention policies.

2) Aggregates
- GET /v1/console/shadow-experiments/{experiment_id}/aggregates
  - Purpose: power the “Quality deltas” and “Health” panels.
  - Query params:
    - window: 1h | 6h | 24h | 7d (default 24h)
    - segment: optional pre-defined segment key (e.g., region, request_type, route_variant_bucket). Must be from allowlist.
    - metrics: optional list of metric keys; defaults to v1 bundle.
  - Response conceptually includes:
    - sample counts (n_control, n_shadow per target)
    - pass/fail rates (format adherence, refusal rate, etc.) per target
    - deltas vs control with confidence intervals (method per Observability Standard)
    - pipeline health indicators (scoring lag p50/p95, missing score rate)
  - Cardinality guardrails:
    - only allow breakdowns on dimension allowlist (no raw prompt_id, no user_id, no customer internal ids)
    - enforce max number of series returned per request (e.g., top K + “other”)

3) Examples (sampled)
- GET /v1/console/shadow-experiments/{experiment_id}/examples
  - Returns a paginated list of scored examples with a stable sampling strategy.
  - Query params:
    - shadow_target_id (required)
    - window (default 24h)
    - outcome filter (regressed | improved | neutral | missing_score | shadow_error)
    - metric_key (optional; used to sort/filter by “worst offenders”)
    - limit (default 20, max 50)
    - cursor
  - Privacy & retention:
    - response payload should return redacted prompt/response fields per retention_profile.
    - examples may include only references (artifact ids) when prompt/response storage is disabled for the tenant.
  - Ordering:
    - default sort: most recent
    - optional sort: highest absolute delta contribution (requires precomputed index; if unavailable, return 400 or fall back)

RBAC & permissions
- All endpoints scoped to tenant derived from auth token.
- Required permissions (names are placeholders; align with Console RBAC system):
  - experiment:read for list/get/aggregates/examples
  - experiment:write for create/edit/pause
  - experiment:delete for archive
  - experiment:editTargets for updating targets after creation
- Additional checks:
  - If route_id is provided, caller must have route:read (and route:write for binding changes).
  - If rollout_id is provided, caller must have rollout:read (and rollout:write if attaching to an active canary).
- Audit logging:
  - Create/update/pause/archive actions emit audit log events with experiment_id, actor, tenant, and diff summary (detailed diff stored server-side; response returns a safe summary).

Data sources / storage
- Control-plane stores experiment definitions (source of truth), but Console API will read from Console DB read model for latency.
- Aggregates are backed by analytics tables derived from shadow telemetry + scoring results (ENG-5404/5405). This ticket includes query-layer plumbing + guardrails, not pipeline creation.
- Examples use a pointer-based model:
  - metadata in analytics store
  - payload in artifact store (if enabled)
  - redaction at write-time + additional redaction at read-time based on role/tenant settings

Edge cases
- Scoring pipeline lagging: aggregates should include “incomplete” flags and missing_score_rate; UI should surface “data still processing.”
- Shadow target errors: count separately (shadow_error_rate) and do not treat as “quality regression,” but do include in health panel.
- Streaming requests: examples may contain partial captures; surface capture_status (partial/complete/timeout) and only compute certain metrics when capture_status=complete.

Acceptance criteria
- CRUD endpoints implemented with validation + proper error messages.
- Aggregates endpoint returns correct values for internal dogfood experiments (validated against notebook queries by Applied ML).
- Examples endpoint respects retention/redaction settings and does not expose raw PII fields.
- RBAC enforced at route/rollout and experiment object levels.
- Audit logs emitted for create/update/pause/archive.
- Load: endpoints remain responsive under high-cardinality tenants; enforce allowlists and series caps.
- Unit + integration tests covering:
  - pagination correctness
  - RBAC denial cases
  - sampling cap enforcement
  - dimension allowlist enforcement

References
- GitHub: sources/github/redwood/pr-24933-console-api-shadow-experiments-crud.json
- Related tickets: ENG-5408 (UI), ENG-5417 (audit logs), ENG-5410 (cardinality guardrails)
- ADRs: shadow routing architecture + telemetry data model/cardinality (Confluence ADRs)

Open questions (tracked here until resolved)
1) Do we allow attaching a shadow experiment to a route without a rollout object in beta? Proposed: yes (route_id supported), but rollout_id required for “show in rollout timeline.”
2) Example payload shape: do we return raw text (redacted) or only artifact refs by default? Proposed default: return redacted text when tenant retention allows; otherwise artifact refs.
3) Confidence intervals: computed in query-time vs precomputed. Proposed: precompute common windows; query-time only for small series counts (guarded).
comments: 2026-01-16 (Dylan Brooks): Creating as P0 for Phase 2 Console beta. UI work (ENG-5408) is blocked until we have stable endpoints + pagination + RBAC semantics. Please coordinate with Jonas/Selene on what metrics must be in aggregates v1.

2026-01-18 (Chloe Martin): Drafted initial API contract (aligning with Drive: shadow-experiments-api-contract-draft). Main concern: aggregates query must be dimension-allowlisted to prevent support escalations like the earlier cardinality incident. Will sync with Allison (Obs) on series caps.

2026-01-22 (Allison Grant): +1 on allowlist + cap. Please do NOT allow arbitrary “tags” query param in v1. We can add a small set of segment keys (region, request_type, model_family) and bucket anything else. Also: include scoring_lag_ms p50/p95 in the aggregates response so dashboards and UI can show “processing delay.”

2026-01-23 (Jonas Weber): For v1 metrics, we need at least: format_adherence_rate, refusal_rate, instruction_following_score (model-graded), safety_flag_rate, and missing_score_rate. Also include sample sizes; we’ve seen small n produce misleading deltas. Confidence intervals should follow the observability standard (Wilson for rates, bootstrap for rubric scores if precomputed).

2026-01-26 (Marcus Lin): Security review note: examples endpoint must enforce retention_profile; do not return raw prompts if the tenant disables storage. Also ensure authZ checks happen before any artifact store lookup to avoid metadata side channels.

2026-01-29 (Chloe Martin): Implemented CRUD + list/get with cursor pagination. Added hard caps: max_targets=3, limit<=100 for list, limit<=50 for examples. Drafted RBAC checks using existing Console policy engine hooks (route:read/rollout:read). Starting aggregates query implementation next; blocked on final metric key names from Applied ML.

2026-02-03 (Selene Huang): Metric keys finalized for v1 bundle: format_adherence_rate, refusal_rate, rubric_overall_score, safety_policy_violation_rate, missing_score_rate. Please expose both absolute values and delta_vs_control + ci_low/ci_high (as floats). If your response schema is strongly typed, ensure we can add new metric keys without breaking older SDKs (map/dictionary).

2026-02-04 (Chloe Martin): We can’t return a map/dictionary in our public API without committing to a schema; but this is Console API (not data plane). Proposal: return metrics as a list of rows {metric_key, control_value, shadow_value, delta, ci_low, ci_high, n}. That keeps it extensible without a map. Will confirm with Monica (SDK).

2026-02-05 (Monica Patel): List-of-rows is good for SDKs. Please ensure metric_key is a stable enum-ish string and add a display_name field in server response for UI convenience (or keep display logic in UI). Prefer not to put display strings in API long-term, but ok for beta if needed.

2026-02-07 (Chloe Martin): PR up for review: implements aggregates + examples endpoints with allowlisted segment keys and series caps. Examples endpoint supports outcome filter and uses artifact refs when payload storage disabled. Added integration tests for RBAC denial + retention gating. PR: redwood/pr-24933.

2026-02-10 (Jada Williams): Rollouts integration: if experiment is created with rollout_id, we should store rollout_phase_id (canary phase) when available so we can later pin metrics to the phase timeline. Not required for beta but please add optional field to create request and store it if present.

2026-02-11 (Chloe Martin): Added optional rollout_phase_id and validated it belongs to rollout_id. Also added audit log hooks behind feature flag (audit schema work in ENG-5417). Merged after approvals.

2026-02-12 (Dylan Brooks): Marking Done. Next: UI integration (ENG-5408) and SDK bindings (ENG-5418). Please ensure docs mention that examples may return artifact refs only depending on tenant retention.
